no88-gap.summary: John Quincy Adams at St Petersburg to the Secretary of State, the day after Napoleon crossed the Niemen: Chancellor Rumyantsev opposed Alexander's journey to Wilna, suffered an apoplectic stroke soon after arriving and a second, worse one since; a German report of his death was false, and JQA judges he cannot long remain at the foreign ministry.
no88-gap.en:
and exp{+ect}ation. But the journey itself of the Emperor {?Alexander} to Wilna was in opposition to the Chancellor's [...] and
{+adv}ice, and if his active influence had not been impa[ir]ed before it, [it] can scarcely fail to have been affected by
his illness immediately after his arrival [there], which was undoubtedly an apoplectic stroke. Since then he has had
a second and a more severe one. In the German Gazettes even his death has been announced; but that was a mistake. At
al[l] event[s] it is scarcely possible that he should remain much longer in the department of foreign affair[s].

100 words, 97 read = 0.970. Holes: {?Alexander}, [...] after Chancellor's, [there].

One-digit slips (the group on the image, the sheet value the word wants):

- exp{+ect}ation: 295 exp, 818 (sheet: del) for 518 ect, 864 ation. The first digit has a closed lower loop like the 8 of 864 beside it;

no88-remainder.summary: The rest of No. 88: a proposal to evacuate Prussia as a preliminary to negotiation would have been neither unreasonable nor offensive; the French ambassador Lauriston took Prince Kurakin's note as proof that Alexander would not negotiate; and JQA expects that early French success would let Napoleon strike directly at the centre of the empire rather than along the Baltic.
no88-remainder.en:
If this proposition has in any form been disclose[d] to the Russian government, it was cer{+tain}ly neither unreasonable
nor immoderate nor inconsistent with a sy[st]em rigorously and {?inflexibly} defensive, to meet it with a proposi[tion]
for the evacuation of Prussia by the French troops as [1508] {?preliminary} {?to} negotiation. But the very point upon
which the {?ambassador} manifested the most sensibility in speaking of Prince Kurakin's last note was that it held out a
{?proposition} with which it would be dishonourable in France to comply. He [1185] it as a demonstration that the Emperor
Alexander had determined not to negotiate at all - it [570] he {?said} - such a proposal as France had never
thought of mak[ing] [to] Russia even after the bat{+tle} of Friedland. [...]

no85-two-lines.summary: After reporting that the English negotiator Thornton has probably pledged his government's consent to the neutrality of Sweden, Adams adds in code that there is some uncertainty how far the neutral intentions and expectations of Sweden herself extend.
no85-two-lines.en:
You will here perceive some uncertainty how far the neutral intention[s] and expectation[s] of Sweden herself extend.

17 words, 15 read = 0.882 (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026: a word with a supplied or emended letter counts as a hole). Holes: intention[s] and expectation[s], whose s is supplied from the plural mark. Read under the short-text floor (README Conventions, 19 Nov 2026: fewer than 40 cipher words, at most 2 holes): 15 of 17, 2 holes.

- intention[s], expectation[s] (two holes: the s is supplied): 1378 and 1369 are each followed on the film by a small raised circle, the plural mark of this code (on frame 0196 the clerk writes "intentions" over 1378 with the same mark). The transcription file does not carry the mark; we028no85.tsv does.
- expectation: 295 exp, 518 ect, 1369 tation (the t is doubled by the syllables).
- extend: 298 ext, 548 end.

no85-three-lines.summary: Adams's comment on Swedish neutrality: if the Regent's new proclamation on the Orders in Council shows what England means by neutrality, and Sweden's meaning of it is shown by her hope of being indemnified with Norway for the loss of Finland, the roots of that neutrality are not very deep.
no85-three-lines.en:
and the Swedish meaning of it is to be [?expounded] by the hope of being {+in}demnified [?in] Norway [?for] the los[s] of Finland …

23 words, 19 read = 0.826 (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026: a word with a supplied or emended letter counts as a hole). Holes: [?expounded], [?in], [?for], los[s]. Read in part.

- [?expounded]: 289 ex, 116x, 520 ed. The first three figures, 116, are clear to three readers; the last is blotted and crossed by a descender from the line above (read 1164 or 1168: we, went, no sense). 1160 pound changes only the blotted figure and answers "elucidate" in the clause before; 1138 plain (ex-plain-ed, the verifier's suggestion) changes the third figure. The sense is the same either way; the word is counted as a hole.
- {+in}demnified: 1310 be, 1429 ing, 1436 (sheet: is) for 1426 in, 821 dem, 439 ni, 335 fied.

no85-foot.summary: The end of the Swedish chargé's assurances to the Emperor Alexander: Finland is separated from the rest of Sweden by a wide gulph, and for its loss Sweden might hope to be indemnified eventually by the acquisition of Norway; the Emperor assured him he would have no objections and make no opposition.
no85-foot.en:
and seperated by so wide and [?extensive] a {+gu}lph from the rest of Sweden — but that for the [?loss] of this {+pro}vince [?Sweden] might perhaps hope to [?be] in{+dem}nified eventually by the acquisition of Norway . . . to which the Emperor assured him that he should have no objection[s], and against which he should make no opposition.

55 words, 50 read = 0.909 (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026: a word with a supplied or emended letter counts as a hole). Holes: [?extensive], [?loss], [?Sweden], [?be], objection[s]. Read in part.

- [?extensive]: 289 ex, 1375 ten, then 23x cut by the binding gutter; 239 sive would finish the word.
- {+gu}lph: 1236 (sheet: ground) for 1238 gu, 1452 l, 1127 ph. 1236 in both blind transcriptions and in the September transcription. 1238 is the group written for gu in con-ti-gu-ous four lines above. One-digit rule.

system: Numerical syllable-and-word code (the = 1385), about 1,600 numbers; 1-100 mostly whole words; values climb alphabetically only in short runs, then break; superscript o = plural, a mark under a group modifies it.
